categories.name: SSD Storage
categories.tagline: Expand console storage for 100+ GB story installs without constant uninstalls.
categories.description: We compare console-friendly internal NVMe drives and plug-and-play externals so you can keep a growing single-player library, day-one patches, and capture clips without deleting games every weekend. Specs focus on what PS5 and Xbox Series actually accept—not PC-only marketing numbers.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 official expansion needs a heatsinked PCIe 4.0 M.2; Xbox Series prefers certified Expansion Cards for internal speed, while USB externals work for archives and media on both.

products.name: WD_BLACK SN850X 2TB with Heatsink
products.summary: The sweet spot for most PS5 owners: official-slot friendly heatsink, real-world speeds that clear Sony’s bar, and enough room for a fat story library plus patches without babysitting storage every week.
products.bestFor: PS5 players who want one install-and-forget internal upgrade
pros: Heatsink model fits the PS5 expansion bay without a separate kit
Consistently clears official console speed requirements
2 TB covers several large titles plus capture overflow
cons: Pricier per TB than bare sticks without a heatsink
Overkill if you only need external archive space

products.name: Samsung T7 Shield 1TB
products.summary: Rugged USB-C portable that works as an external game library and media dump on both PS5 and Xbox Series. Not a replacement for official internal expansion speed, but the best “plug it in and stop deleting games” move under $100.
products.bestFor: Players who want zero internal installs and quick offloads
pros: USB-C plug-and-play on PS5 and Xbox Series
IP65-rated shell survives couch and travel chaos
Fast enough for external game installs and media
cons: Won’t match internal NVMe load times
1 TB fills up fast with multiple 100 GB titles

products.name: Seagate FireCuda 530 4TB Heatsink
products.summary: Buy-once capacity for collectors and creators: 4 TB of heatsinked NVMe so you can keep a full console library, large day-one patches, and long capture projects without juggling uninstalls.
products.bestFor: Heavy libraries, capture hobbies, and “never delete again” setups
pros: 4 TB headroom for a full modern console library
Heatsinked variant aimed at console expansion bays
Rescue Data Recovery plan included on many SKUs
cons: Premium price; wait for sales if budget-sensitive
Physically larger heatsink—confirm bay clearance

categories.name: Headsets
categories.tagline: Hear story dialogue and positional cues without drowning the mix.
categories.description: Console-first headsets ranked for long-session comfort, mic clarity for party chat, and dialogue-friendly tuning. We prioritize connections that work on PS5 and Xbox Series without PC-only software or proprietary ecosystems you cannot leave.
categories.consoleAngle: Confirm 3.5 mm, USB-C, Xbox Wireless, or licensed wireless dongles—many “gaming” headsets still need PC software for EQ and will disappoint on console day one.

products.name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7P
products.summary: Wireless comfort with a clear center image for dialogue-heavy story games and a flip-to-mute boom that works in party chat. Dual wireless (2.4 GHz + Bluetooth) means you can take a call without yanking the dongle out of the DualSense.
products.bestFor: PS5 story sessions with occasional party chat
pros: Lightweight for multi-hour campaigns
2.4 GHz + Bluetooth dual link
Flip-to-mute boom and solid battery life
cons: Xbox needs the Xbox-specific Nova variant
App EQ is nicer on PC than on console

specs.platformNotes: Nova 7P for PlayStation; use 7X on Xbox

products.name: HyperX Cloud Stinger 2
products.summary: Wired reliability for story nights: no battery anxiety, a usable boom mic, and soft enough pads for a long campaign. The 3.5 mm jack works with DualSense, Xbox controllers, and most TV headphone outs.
products.bestFor: Budget console players who want simple and durable
pros: Works on any console with a 3.5 mm jack
No batteries or dongles to lose
Swappable ear cushions extend lifespan
cons: Stereo only—no wireless freedom
Mic is fine for chat, not streaming

specs.platformNotes: Controller jack on PS5 / Xbox / Switch

products.name: Sony INZONE H9
products.summary: Premium pads and active noise canceling for immersion without blasting volume—especially useful in noisy apartments when you still want to catch quiet story beats. Spatial audio tuning and a broadcast-leaning mic round out a high-end PS5-friendly kit.
products.bestFor: Immersion-first PS5 players in noisy rooms
pros: ANC helps keep volumes reasonable
Plush pads for marathon sessions
Strong spatial audio story experience
cons: Pricey; ANC is less useful on quiet couches
Xbox support is more limited than PS5

specs.platformNotes: Best on PS5 / PC; limited Xbox wireless

categories.name: TVs & Monitors
categories.tagline: Display picks tuned for console HDMI 2.1, VRR, and HDR story nights.
categories.description: Side-by-side TVs and monitors that make sense for couch or desk console play. We prioritize ALLM, VRR, 4K120 where it matters, and HDR that still looks good in a normal living room—without chasing PC-only features your console cannot use.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 and Xbox Series shine on HDMI 2.1 ports with VRR and ALLM. A 120 Hz panel only helps if the console and the game mode path actually deliver it.

products.name: LG C4 55" OLED evo
products.summary: The living-room default for console story games: perfect blacks, four full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports, and a Game Optimizer path that enables VRR and ALLM without menu spelunking. 55" fits most apartments without dominating the wall.
products.bestFor: Couch PS5 / Xbox play in a light-controlled room
pros: Four HDMI 2.1 ports for console + soundbar + more
Excellent contrast for cinematic single-player
Mature game mode with VRR / ALLM
cons: Brightness limited in bright daytime rooms
Burn-in risk if you leave static HUDs for years

products.name: LG UltraGear 27GR75Q-B 27"
products.summary: Desk-friendly 1440p monitor for sharper HUD text and competitive clarity on a budget. HDMI 2.0 caps pure 4K120 dreams, but console VRR support and a fast IPS panel make it a strong “bedroom / office console” pick.
products.bestFor: Desk or dorm setups where 27" beats a huge TV
pros: Sharp 1440p text and HUDs
High refresh for smoother camera pans
Console VRR via Adaptive-Sync path
cons: Not a 4K living-room TV replacement
HDR is modest compared with OLED TVs

products.name: Samsung QN90D 65" Neo QLED
products.summary: Bright Mini-LED punch for daytime rooms where OLEDs can look washed out. Full console gaming feature set with 4K120 and VRR, plus a larger canvas for couch co-op and cinematic set pieces.
products.bestFor: Bright living rooms that still want 4K120 gaming
pros: Excellent peak brightness for sunny rooms
65" shared-view size for couch sessions
Strong 4K120 + VRR console support
cons: Contrast can’t match OLED in dark rooms
Premium pricing—shop holiday sales

categories.name: Capture Cards
categories.tagline: Record and stream console footage without turning your living room into a PC LAN.
categories.description: Capture cards for creators who play on console and need clean HDMI pass-through to a streaming PC or laptop. We rank for latency, HDR pass-through honesty, and USB convenience—no unofficial firmware, no console mods.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 and Xbox Series both output HDMI; you need a card that can pass 4K60 HDR to the TV while capturing a usable stream resolution to the PC.

products.name: Elgato HD60 X
products.summary: The creator default: reliable 4K60 HDR pass-through with 1080p60 (VRR-aware) capture over USB-C. Works with PS5 and Xbox Series without weird adapters, and pairs cleanly with OBS / Stream Deck workflows.
products.bestFor: Most console streamers and highlight editors
pros: Solid 4K60 HDR pass-through to your TV
USB-C convenience—no PCIe slot required
Mature Elgato software + OBS support
cons: Native capture tops out below 4K60
Needs a capable USB port and CPU for encoding

products.name: AverMedia Live Gamer Mini
products.summary: Simple 1080p capture for Discord clips, TikTok highlights, and learning OBS without spending creator-tax money. Fine for SDR console footage when you do not need 4K HDR pass-through.
products.bestFor: First-time clip creators on a tight budget
pros: Affordable entry into console capture
USB stick form factor travels easily
Works for basic 1080p highlight reels
cons: No premium HDR / 4K60 pass-through path
Capture limited versus HD60-class cards

products.name: Elgato 4K60 Pro MK.2
products.summary: Internal PCIe capture when you already have a desktop and want the cleanest 4K60 path with lower USB overhead. Best for serious console creators who edit in 4K and keep a dedicated streaming PC under the desk.
pros: True 4K60 capture for high-end workflows
PCIe reduces USB bandwidth drama
HDR-capable capture path
cons: Requires a desktop with a free PCIe slot
Overkill for casual Discord clips
